headline: Kenner Tatooine Skiff found for eight dollars
post:
A lucky Star Wars fan reportedly snagged a rare Kenner Tatooine Skiff at a thrift store for only $8.49. That vehicle normally commands a price between $800 and $1,200 depending on its condition.

This incredible piece even came with all its rails and supports in place. Commenters on Reddit could scarcely believe such a massive bargain actually happened in the wild.

headline: The Dark Knight Batpod auction nears one million
post:
Christian Bale's actual Batpod from The Dark Knight and The Dark Knight Rises is currently heading toward a staggering one million dollars at auction. This two-wheeled ride comes with distinct scratches that match the memorable scene where Batman narrowly avoids Heath Ledger's Joker. It is sold in rolling only condition because the fuel tank, throttle controls, and battery were removed.

headline: Batman storylines that changed the DC universe
post:
Batman has evolved across decades from a pulp detective into the psychological cornerstone of the DC universe, with landmark arcs that reshaped his entire mythos. According to Screen Rant, iconic narrative runs have repeatedly driven major structural changes throughout DC continuity by testing the Dark Knight's limits and redefining his allies.

From Frank Miller and David Mazzucchelli redefining his beginnings to Alan Moore exploring the Joker's philosophy, these classic tales permanently altered comic history. Readers have witnessed devastating tragedies like the loss of Jason Todd alongside massive status quo shifts that introduced unforgettable new characters to the mainstream.

headline: Skydance taps Jeremy Latcham as new DC Studios head
post:
Big changes are coming to the DC Universe after a corporate merger under Skydance led James Gunn and Peter Safran to step down as co-heads, according to /Film. Skydance CEO David Ellison reportedly wants to completely dismantle Gunn's universe and end the Gods and Monsters chapter early. To lead this reinvention, former Marvel producer Jeremy Latcham has been installed as the new president and chief creative officer of DC Studios. Meanwhile, DC Comics has been brought under Skydance's products and publishing team, giving Jim Lee more opportunity to influence the cinematic side of the studio going forward. Latcham brings extensive blockbuster experience and a preference for family-friendly entertainment, though plenty of projects currently in production still need to be evaluated by the new leadership. Gunn is still attached to direct his Superman sequel "Man of Tomorrow," which is slated for release on July 9, 2027. What are your thoughts on this major leadership shakeup for DC? 

#DCStudios #JamesGunn #DCUniverse
original_title: ​​Big Changes Are Coming To The DC Universe In 2027
